transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I guess I'm here because... ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself. 

I've been finding myself crying over silly things, like the potluck lists. And I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle easy. I've even started missing church planning things, which is something I never, ever would have missed before. I just don't feel right, and I thought I better come in and talk to someone.
Since your friend passed away, have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like choir or other activities?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still care very much about the choir and all the church activities. 

It's more that... well, I just get so overwhelmed or emotional lately that I end up staying home. I still want to be involved, but when it actually comes time to go, I just can't seem to manage it right now. So the interest is definitely still there, it's just hard for me to participate the way I used to.
Have you noticed that most days, you feel down or sad, even when you're not thinking about your friend passing away?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down most days. It's really just when something reminds me of her, or when I'm trying to deal with the church stuff we used to do together. If I'm just going about my normal day around the house, I feel fine. It's not like a dark cloud hanging over me all the time, it's just... those specific moments that get to me.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious, restless, or on edge lately, even when there’s no specific reminder of your friend or church activities?

No, not really. I mean... I don't feel jumpy or on edge just sitting around the house. If I'm doing my regular chores or, you know, watching a show, I feel perfectly calm. 

It really just hits me when those specific reminders pop up, like I mentioned before. But otherwise, no, I haven't noticed feeling restless or anxious out of nowhere.
Outside of the specific reminders of your friend or church activities, have you noticed any lasting changes in your mood, energy, or ability to enjoy life over the past few weeks?

No, not really. Aside from those moments when I'm reminded of her or the church activities, my mood and energy are pretty much the same as always. I still enjoy my day-to-day life, like working in the garden or reading a book. It's just those specific triggers that throw me off, but otherwise, everything feels pretty normal.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or lost pleasure in activities, even outside of the moments that remind you of your friend or church activities?

No, um... I think we just touched on that, but no, I really haven't. Like I said, outside of those specific moments, I haven't had days where I just feel down or can't enjoy things. My day-to-day life is fine, and I still get plenty of enjoyment out of my regular activities.
Have you had any feelings of worthlessness or guilt that don’t seem connected to specific reminders of your friend or church activities?

No, not at all. I don't feel worthless... or guilty. It's really just like I was saying a minute ago. As long as those specific reminders don't come up, I feel perfectly fine about myself and my life. I haven't had any feelings like that.
Since your friend passed away, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels specifically when you're reminded of her or dealing with church-related tasks?

No, not really. I mean, when I get upset about it, I might cry or feel a little drained right in that moment, but it doesn't really mess up my sleep or change how much I eat. My energy is fine once the moment passes.
Have you had trouble functioning normally in any part of your life, like at home or with other people, when you aren't thinking about your friend or church activities?

No, I haven't. Everything else is... well, it's normal. I take care of the house, I see my family, I talk to my neighbors. I don't have any trouble doing the things I need to do, as long as it's not related to the church or... or her.
How long have these emotional reactions been happening since your friend passed away, and have they stayed just as intense over time or changed in any way?

It's been going on for about a month now. That's when my close choir friend died. And... well, it hasn't really changed or gotten any easier. The reactions feel just as intense now as they did right after it happened, whenever those specific reminders come up.
When you're not being reminded of your friend or church activities, do you still find yourself thinking about her a lot or feeling a strong sense of longing for her presence?

No, not really. If I'm just going about my day and there's no reason for me to think about the church or her passing... I don't really dwell on it. I mean, I miss her, of course, but I'm not sitting around just longing for her or thinking about it constantly if something hasn't reminded me.
Even when you're not reminded of your friend or involved in church activities, do you find yourself frequently thinking about her death or wishing she were still here?

No, I don't think so. Like I said, if I'm not doing anything related to the church or... or reminded of her, I'm not really focused on it. I mean, I wish she hadn't passed, but I don't spend my day just thinking about her death or wishing she was here, unless something brings it up.
Have you noticed any difficulty moving on or a sense that you’re stuck in your grief, even when you’re not being reminded of your friend or the church activities?

No, I wouldn't say I feel stuck. Like I was just saying, when I'm away from the church and those reminders, I'm really just going about my normal day. I don't feel like I'm having trouble moving forward in my day-to-day life... it's really just those specific moments that hit me hard. Otherwise, I'm doing okay.
When those specific reminders of your friend or church activities come up, how intense do your emotional reactions feel, and how long do they usually last once they start?

Well, when I'm reminded of her... the feelings are definitely strong. It makes me really sad, and sometimes I get a bit teary. But as for how long it lasts... I'm not really sure. I haven't timed it or anything. I guess it just lasts until I can kind of gather myself and move on to whatever else I need to do.

When you're reminded of your friend or the church activities you used to do together, do those emotional reactions tend to last for a long time, like most of the day, or do they usually pass more quickly?

They usually pass pretty quickly, to be honest. It's not like it ruins the whole day or anything. I might feel really down for a few minutes, maybe shed a tear, but then I just... I don't know, I just get back to whatever I was doing. It definitely doesn't last all day.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests adjustment disorder with depressed mood, mild depressive episode, and uncomplicated bereavement. Further questioning is needed to clarify duration, intensity, and context of symptoms.

Ruled out F32.0 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, mild) due to the patient reporting that they do not feel down or sad most days, which is inconsistent with the persistent sadness required for a depressive disorder. The grief response appears to be more specific to reminders of the deceased friend and situational stressors, supporting adjustment disorder (F43.22) or prolonged grief disorder (F43.10).
